behavior.explanation: The endpoint binds the caller through Depends(get_verified_user), then authorizes selection of the supplied file_id by role: admins look up any file by ID, while non-admins use a lookup constrained by both file_id and user.id. If a file is selected, the destination is the supplied collection_name or the derived name file-{file.id}. The handler processes content and updates the selected file; unless retrieval is bypassed, it passes that destination to the vector helper, which can insert vectors there. No destination-collection authorization check is visible in the traced flow.

observations.subject: process_file route
observations.claim: The entry is POST /process/file in retrieval.py, included by main.py under the /api/v1/retrieval router prefix; the handler requires form_data and a verified user dependency.

observations.subject: verified caller
observations.claim: The caller is the user object supplied by Depends(get_verified_user); the handler branches on user.role and uses user.id for non-admin file selection.

observations.subject: supplied file_id
observations.claim: The supplied form_data.file_id selects the file. Admin callers fetch by file ID alone; non-admin callers fetch by file ID together with user.id, so the non-admin lookup is directly owner-bound.

observations.subject: file existence and caller branch
observations.claim: Processing proceeds only if the selected file is truthy. Admin role permits lookup without an owner predicate; all other roles use the owner-constrained lookup. A missing or unauthorized non-admin selection reaches the same visible not-found response branch.

observations.subject: destination collection_name
observations.claim: The destination is form_data.collection_name when supplied; otherwise it is derived as file-{file.id}. The supplied collection name is not used in the file-selection guard.

observations.subject: processing and vector write
observations.claim: After file selection, the handler builds documents from supplied content, previously stored vector content, a loader over file.path, or file.data. It updates the selected file's content/status/hash and, when embedding/retrieval is enabled, calls save_docs_to_vector_db with the selected collection_name and metadata containing the selected file.id; that function ultimately inserts vector items into that collection.

observations.subject: shared-file access helper
observations.claim: retrieval.py imports has_access_to_file, but the visible process_file body does not call it. The helper itself supports ownership and several sharing relationships, but its documented use is not evidenced on this path.

observations.subject: same selected file
observations.claim: The input object is the file selected from form_data.file_id. The handler uses that same file.id for document metadata, file-data updates, final metadata/status/hash updates, and the vector-write metadata.

observations.subject: collection versus file
observations.claim: The file identity and collection identity are distinct: file.id identifies the authorized/selected file, while collection_name may be caller-supplied and may name a collection unrelated by source-visible authorization to that file.

observations.subject: output target
observations.claim: The protected input object and file-record effects are the same selected file, but the vector effect targets the separately chosen collection_name. Therefore input-file identity and all output targets are not uniformly the same object.

observations.subject: ownership scenarios
observations.claim: Both scenarios enter the same POST handler and are subject to the admin/non-admin file lookup branch before processing.

observations.subject: caller-owned file
observations.claim: For a non-admin caller whose user.id equals the file's owner identity used by get_file_by_id_and_user_id, the file is selected and processing can continue, subject to the later processing and configuration conditions.

observations.subject: file owned by another user
observations.claim: For a non-admin caller and a file owned by another user, the owner-constrained lookup does not select that file on the visible path, so the handler raises HTTP 404 and does not reach processing or vector insertion. The source does not show a sharing/access-grant exception in this handler.

observations.subject: admin caller
observations.claim: An admin caller is an explicit exception: the handler fetches by file ID without the non-admin owner predicate, so an existing file owned by another user can proceed. This does not establish any destination-collection ownership or authorization.

observations.subject: destination collection
observations.claim: Caller ownership of the file does not imply ownership of form_data.collection_name. The visible process_file path does not check collection ownership or collection access before passing the name to vector operations.

observations.subject: successful owned-file path
observations.claim: When processing succeeds, the selected file record is updated and vector items can be inserted into the supplied collection or the derived file-{file.id} collection, depending on the request and configuration.

observations.subject: content and collection branches
observations.claim: Visible branches are: supplied content takes precedence and deletes the file-{file.id} async vector collection before rebuilding docs; a supplied collection without content first queries file-{file.id} for prior content and otherwise uses file.data; with neither, the handler loads from storage when file.path exists or uses file.data.

observations.subject: bypass configuration
observations.claim: If BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is enabled, the handler updates file status/hash and returns success without calling save_docs_to_vector_db; the returned collection_name is None.

observations.subject: vector-write conditions
observations.claim: When bypass is disabled, save_docs_to_vector_db may return early if the destination collection already exists and add is false; add is true only when form_data.collection_name was supplied. Otherwise it generates embeddings and inserts items into the named collection.

observations.subject: duplicate and content limits
observations.claim: The vector helper checks an existing document hash and raises a duplicate-content error when the existing metadata file_id differs; empty post-split documents and invalid splitter configuration also fail before insertion.

observations.subject: failure behavior
observations.claim: Processing exceptions update the selected file status to failed and clear its hash, then return an HTTP 400 for the visible handler-level error path; a missing selected file returns HTTP 404.

observations.subject: authorization limits
observations.claim: The visible authorization limit is file selection by admin role or exact caller ownership lookup for non-admins. No destination collection authorization, collection-owner binding, or invocation of the imported generalized file-access helper is shown in this path.

observations.subject: process_file route
observations.claim: The entry is POST /process/file in retrieval.py, included by main.py under the /api/v1/retrieval router prefix; the handler requires form_data and a verified user dependency.

observations.subject: verified caller
observations.claim: The caller is the user object supplied by Depends(get_verified_user); the handler branches on user.role and uses user.id for non-admin file selection.

observations.subject: supplied file_id
observations.claim: The supplied form_data.file_id selects the file. Admin callers fetch by file ID alone; non-admin callers fetch by file ID together with user.id, so the non-admin lookup is directly owner-bound.

observations.subject: file existence and caller branch
observations.claim: Processing proceeds only if the selected file is truthy. Admin role permits lookup without an owner predicate; all other roles use the owner-constrained lookup. A missing or unauthorized non-admin selection reaches the same visible not-found response branch.

observations.subject: destination collection_name
observations.claim: The destination is form_data.collection_name when supplied; otherwise it is derived as file-{file.id}. The supplied collection name is not used in the file-selection guard.

observations.subject: processing and vector write
observations.claim: After file selection, the handler builds documents from supplied content, previously stored vector content, a loader over file.path, or file.data. It updates the selected file's content/status/hash and, when embedding/retrieval is enabled, calls save_docs_to_vector_db with the selected collection_name and metadata containing the selected file.id; that function ultimately inserts vector items into that collection.

observations.subject: shared-file access helper
observations.claim: retrieval.py imports has_access_to_file, but the visible process_file body does not call it. The helper itself supports ownership and several sharing relationships, but its documented use is not evidenced on this path.

observations.subject: same selected file
observations.claim: The input object is the file selected from form_data.file_id. The handler uses that same file.id for document metadata, file-data updates, final metadata/status/hash updates, and the vector-write metadata.

observations.subject: collection versus file
observations.claim: The file identity and collection identity are distinct: file.id identifies the authorized/selected file, while collection_name may be caller-supplied and may name a collection unrelated by source-visible authorization to that file.

observations.subject: output target
observations.claim: The protected input object and file-record effects are the same selected file, but the vector effect targets the separately chosen collection_name. Therefore input-file identity and all output targets are not uniformly the same object.

observations.subject: ownership scenarios
observations.claim: Both scenarios enter the same POST handler and are subject to the admin/non-admin file lookup branch before processing.

observations.subject: caller-owned file
observations.claim: For a non-admin caller whose user.id equals the file's owner identity used by get_file_by_id_and_user_id, the file is selected and processing can continue, subject to the later processing and configuration conditions.

observations.subject: file owned by another user
observations.claim: For a non-admin caller and a file owned by another user, the owner-constrained lookup does not select that file on the visible path, so the handler raises HTTP 404 and does not reach processing or vector insertion. The source does not show a sharing/access-grant exception in this handler.

observations.subject: admin caller
observations.claim: An admin caller is an explicit exception: the handler fetches by file ID without the non-admin owner predicate, so an existing file owned by another user can proceed. This does not establish any destination-collection ownership or authorization.

observations.subject: destination collection
observations.claim: Caller ownership of the file does not imply ownership of form_data.collection_name. The visible process_file path does not check collection ownership or collection access before passing the name to vector operations.

observations.subject: successful owned-file path
observations.claim: When processing succeeds, the selected file record is updated and vector items can be inserted into the supplied collection or the derived file-{file.id} collection, depending on the request and configuration.

observations.subject: content and collection branches
observations.claim: Visible branches are: supplied content takes precedence and deletes the file-{file.id} async vector collection before rebuilding docs; a supplied collection without content first queries file-{file.id} for prior content and otherwise uses file.data; with neither, the handler loads from storage when file.path exists or uses file.data.

observations.subject: bypass configuration
observations.claim: If BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is enabled, the handler updates file status/hash and returns success without calling save_docs_to_vector_db; the returned collection_name is None.

observations.subject: vector-write conditions
observations.claim: When bypass is disabled, save_docs_to_vector_db may return early if the destination collection already exists and add is false; add is true only when form_data.collection_name was supplied. Otherwise it generates embeddings and inserts items into the named collection.

observations.subject: duplicate and content limits
observations.claim: The vector helper checks an existing document hash and raises a duplicate-content error when the existing metadata file_id differs; empty post-split documents and invalid splitter configuration also fail before insertion.

observations.subject: failure behavior
observations.claim: Processing exceptions update the selected file status to failed and clear its hash, then return an HTTP 400 for the visible handler-level error path; a missing selected file returns HTTP 404.

observations.subject: authorization limits
observations.claim: The visible authorization limit is file selection by admin role or exact caller ownership lookup for non-admins. No destination collection authorization, collection-owner binding, or invocation of the imported generalized file-access helper is shown in this path.

observations.subject: process_file route
observations.claim: The entry is POST /process/file in retrieval.py, included by main.py under the /api/v1/retrieval router prefix; the handler requires form_data and a verified user dependency.

observations.subject: verified caller
observations.claim: The caller is the user object supplied by Depends(get_verified_user); the handler branches on user.role and uses user.id for non-admin file selection.

observations.subject: supplied file_id
observations.claim: The supplied form_data.file_id selects the file. Admin callers fetch by file ID alone; non-admin callers fetch by file ID together with user.id, so the non-admin lookup is directly owner-bound.

observations.subject: file existence and caller branch
observations.claim: Processing proceeds only if the selected file is truthy. Admin role permits lookup without an owner predicate; all other roles use the owner-constrained lookup. A missing or unauthorized non-admin selection reaches the same visible not-found response branch.

observations.subject: destination collection_name
observations.claim: The destination is form_data.collection_name when supplied; otherwise it is derived as file-{file.id}. The supplied collection name is not used in the file-selection guard.

observations.subject: processing and vector write
observations.claim: After file selection, the handler builds documents from supplied content, previously stored vector content, a loader over file.path, or file.data. It updates the selected file's content/status/hash and, when embedding/retrieval is enabled, calls save_docs_to_vector_db with the selected collection_name and metadata containing the selected file.id; that function ultimately inserts vector items into that collection.

observations.subject: shared-file access helper
observations.claim: retrieval.py imports has_access_to_file, but the visible process_file body does not call it. The helper itself supports ownership and several sharing relationships, but its documented use is not evidenced on this path.

observations.subject: same selected file
observations.claim: The input object is the file selected from form_data.file_id. The handler uses that same file.id for document metadata, file-data updates, final metadata/status/hash updates, and the vector-write metadata.

observations.subject: collection versus file
observations.claim: The file identity and collection identity are distinct: file.id identifies the authorized/selected file, while collection_name may be caller-supplied and may name a collection unrelated by source-visible authorization to that file.

observations.subject: output target
observations.claim: The protected input object and file-record effects are the same selected file, but the vector effect targets the separately chosen collection_name. Therefore input-file identity and all output targets are not uniformly the same object.

observations.subject: ownership scenarios
observations.claim: Both scenarios enter the same POST handler and are subject to the admin/non-admin file lookup branch before processing.

observations.subject: caller-owned file
observations.claim: For a non-admin caller whose user.id equals the file's owner identity used by get_file_by_id_and_user_id, the file is selected and processing can continue, subject to the later processing and configuration conditions.

observations.subject: file owned by another user
observations.claim: For a non-admin caller and a file owned by another user, the owner-constrained lookup does not select that file on the visible path, so the handler raises HTTP 404 and does not reach processing or vector insertion. The source does not show a sharing/access-grant exception in this handler.

observations.subject: admin caller
observations.claim: An admin caller is an explicit exception: the handler fetches by file ID without the non-admin owner predicate, so an existing file owned by another user can proceed. This does not establish any destination-collection ownership or authorization.

observations.subject: destination collection
observations.claim: Caller ownership of the file does not imply ownership of form_data.collection_name. The visible process_file path does not check collection ownership or collection access before passing the name to vector operations.

observations.subject: successful owned-file path
observations.claim: When processing succeeds, the selected file record is updated and vector items can be inserted into the supplied collection or the derived file-{file.id} collection, depending on the request and configuration.

observations.subject: content and collection branches
observations.claim: Visible branches are: supplied content takes precedence and deletes the file-{file.id} async vector collection before rebuilding docs; a supplied collection without content first queries file-{file.id} for prior content and otherwise uses file.data; with neither, the handler loads from storage when file.path exists or uses file.data.

observations.subject: bypass configuration
observations.claim: If BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is enabled, the handler updates file status/hash and returns success without calling save_docs_to_vector_db; the returned collection_name is None.

observations.subject: vector-write conditions
observations.claim: When bypass is disabled, save_docs_to_vector_db may return early if the destination collection already exists and add is false; add is true only when form_data.collection_name was supplied. Otherwise it generates embeddings and inserts items into the named collection.

observations.subject: duplicate and content limits
observations.claim: The vector helper checks an existing document hash and raises a duplicate-content error when the existing metadata file_id differs; empty post-split documents and invalid splitter configuration also fail before insertion.

observations.subject: failure behavior
observations.claim: Processing exceptions update the selected file status to failed and clear its hash, then return an HTTP 400 for the visible handler-level error path; a missing selected file returns HTTP 404.

observations.subject: authorization limits
observations.claim: The visible authorization limit is file selection by admin role or exact caller ownership lookup for non-admins. No destination collection authorization, collection-owner binding, or invocation of the imported generalized file-access helper is shown in this path.

18 |     file_id: str | None,
19 |     access_type: str,
20 |     user: UserModel,
21 |     db: AsyncSession | None = None,
22 | ) -> bool:
23 |     """
24 |     Check if a user has the specified access to a file through any of:
25 |     - Knowledge bases (ownership or access grants)
26 |     - Shared workspace models that attach the file directly
27 |     - Channels the user is a member of
28 |     - Shared chats
29 | 
30 |     NOTE: This does NOT check direct file ownership — callers should check
31 |     file.user_id == user.id separately before calling this.
32 |     """
33 |     file = await Files.get_file_by_id(file_id, db=db)
34 |     log.debug(f'Checking if user has {access_type} access to file')
35 |     if not file:
36 |         return False
37 | 
38 |     # Direct ownership
39 |     if file.user_id == user.id:
40 |         return True
41 | 
42 |     # Check if the file is associated with any knowledge bases the user has access to
43 |     knowledge_bases = await Knowledges.get_knowledges_by_file_id(file_id, db=db)
44 |     user_group_ids = {group.id for group in await Groups.get_groups_by_member_id(user.id, db=db)}
45 |     for knowledge_base in knowledge_bases:
46 |         if knowledge_base.user_id == user.id or await AccessGrants.has_access(
47 |             user_id=user.id,
48 |             resource_type='knowledge',
49 |             resource_id=knowledge_base.id,
50 |             permission=access_type,
51 |             user_group_ids=user_group_ids,
52 |             db=db,
53 |         ):
54 |             return True
55 | 
56 |     knowledge_base_id = file.meta.get('collection_name') if file.meta else None
57 |     if knowledge_base_id:
58 |         knowledge_bases = await Knowledges.get_knowledge_bases_by_user_id(user.id, access_type, db=db)
59 |         for knowledge_base in knowledge_bases:
60 |             if knowledge_base.id == knowledge_base_id:
61 |                 return True
62 | 
63 |     # Check if the file is associated with any channels the user has access to
64 |     channels = await Channels.get_channels_by_file_id_and_user_id(file_id, user.id, db=db)
65 |     if access_type == 'read' and channels:
66 |         return True
67 | 
68 |     # Check if the file is associated with any chats the user has access to
69 |     shared_chat_ids = await Chats.get_shared_chat_ids_by_file_id(file_id, db=db)
70 |     if shared_chat_ids:
71 |         accessible_ids = await AccessGrants.get_accessible_resource_ids(
72 |             user_id=user.id,
73 |             resource_type='shared_chat',
74 |             resource_ids=shared_chat_ids,
75 |             permission='read',
76 |             user_group_ids=user_group_ids,
77 |             db=db,
78 |         )
79 |         if accessible_ids:
80 |             return True
81 | 
82 |     # Check if the file is directly attached to a shared workspace model
83 |     for model in await Models.get_models_by_user_id(user.id, permission=access_type, db=db):
84 |         knowledge_items = getattr(model.meta, 'knowledge', None) or []
85 |         for item in knowledge_items:
86 |             if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get('type') == 'file' and item.get('id') == file.id:
87 |                 return True
88 | 
89 |     return False

18 |     file_id: str | None,
19 |     access_type: str,
20 |     user: UserModel,
21 |     db: AsyncSession | None = None,
22 | ) -> bool:
23 |     """
24 |     Check if a user has the specified access to a file through any of:
25 |     - Knowledge bases (ownership or access grants)
26 |     - Shared workspace models that attach the file directly
27 |     - Channels the user is a member of
28 |     - Shared chats
29 | 
30 |     NOTE: This does NOT check direct file ownership — callers should check
31 |     file.user_id == user.id separately before calling this.
32 |     """
33 |     file = await Files.get_file_by_id(file_id, db=db)
34 |     log.debug(f'Checking if user has {access_type} access to file')
35 |     if not file:
36 |         return False
37 | 
38 |     # Direct ownership
39 |     if file.user_id == user.id:
40 |         return True
41 | 
42 |     # Check if the file is associated with any knowledge bases the user has access to
43 |     knowledge_bases = await Knowledges.get_knowledges_by_file_id(file_id, db=db)
44 |     user_group_ids = {group.id for group in await Groups.get_groups_by_member_id(user.id, db=db)}
45 |     for knowledge_base in knowledge_bases:
46 |         if knowledge_base.user_id == user.id or await AccessGrants.has_access(
47 |             user_id=user.id,
48 |             resource_type='knowledge',
49 |             resource_id=knowledge_base.id,
50 |             permission=access_type,
51 |             user_group_ids=user_group_ids,
52 |             db=db,
53 |         ):
54 |             return True
55 | 
56 |     knowledge_base_id = file.meta.get('collection_name') if file.meta else None
57 |     if knowledge_base_id:
58 |         knowledge_bases = await Knowledges.get_knowledge_bases_by_user_id(user.id, access_type, db=db)
59 |         for knowledge_base in knowledge_bases:
60 |             if knowledge_base.id == knowledge_base_id:
61 |                 return True
62 | 
63 |     # Check if the file is associated with any channels the user has access to
64 |     channels = await Channels.get_channels_by_file_id_and_user_id(file_id, user.id, db=db)
65 |     if access_type == 'read' and channels:
66 |         return True
67 | 
68 |     # Check if the file is associated with any chats the user has access to
69 |     shared_chat_ids = await Chats.get_shared_chat_ids_by_file_id(file_id, db=db)
70 |     if shared_chat_ids:
71 |         accessible_ids = await AccessGrants.get_accessible_resource_ids(
72 |             user_id=user.id,
73 |             resource_type='shared_chat',
74 |             resource_ids=shared_chat_ids,
75 |             permission='read',
76 |             user_group_ids=user_group_ids,
77 |             db=db,
78 |         )
79 |         if accessible_ids:
80 |             return True
81 | 
82 |     # Check if the file is directly attached to a shared workspace model
83 |     for model in await Models.get_models_by_user_id(user.id, permission=access_type, db=db):
84 |         knowledge_items = getattr(model.meta, 'knowledge', None) or []
85 |         for item in knowledge_items:
86 |             if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get('type') == 'file' and item.get('id') == file.id:
87 |                 return True
88 | 
89 |     return False

269 |     def _glob_to_like_pattern(glob: str) -> str:
270 |         """
271 |         Convert a glob/fnmatch pattern to a SQL LIKE pattern.
272 | 
273 |         Escapes SQL special characters and converts glob wildcards:
274 |         - `*` becomes `%` (match any sequence of characters)
275 |         - `?` becomes `_` (match exactly one character)
276 | 
277 |         Args:
278 |             glob: A glob pattern (e.g., "*.txt", "file?.doc")
279 | 
280 |         Returns:
281 |             A SQL LIKE compatible pattern with proper escaping.
282 |         """
283 |         # Escape SQL special characters first, then convert glob wildcards
284 |         pattern = glob.replace('\\', '\\\\')
285 |         pattern = pattern.replace('%', '\\%')
286 |         pattern = pattern.replace('_', '\\_')
287 |         pattern = pattern.replace('*', '%')
288 |         pattern = pattern.replace('?', '_')
289 |         return pattern

18 |     file_id: str | None,
19 |     access_type: str,
20 |     user: UserModel,
21 |     db: AsyncSession | None = None,
22 | ) -> bool:
23 |     """
24 |     Check if a user has the specified access to a file through any of:
25 |     - Knowledge bases (ownership or access grants)
26 |     - Shared workspace models that attach the file directly
27 |     - Channels the user is a member of
28 |     - Shared chats
29 | 
30 |     NOTE: This does NOT check direct file ownership — callers should check
31 |     file.user_id == user.id separately before calling this.
32 |     """
33 |     file = await Files.get_file_by_id(file_id, db=db)
34 |     log.debug(f'Checking if user has {access_type} access to file')
35 |     if not file:
36 |         return False
37 | 
38 |     # Direct ownership
39 |     if file.user_id == user.id:
40 |         return True
41 | 
42 |     # Check if the file is associated with any knowledge bases the user has access to
43 |     knowledge_bases = await Knowledges.get_knowledges_by_file_id(file_id, db=db)
44 |     user_group_ids = {group.id for group in await Groups.get_groups_by_member_id(user.id, db=db)}
45 |     for knowledge_base in knowledge_bases:
46 |         if knowledge_base.user_id == user.id or await AccessGrants.has_access(
47 |             user_id=user.id,
48 |             resource_type='knowledge',
49 |             resource_id=knowledge_base.id,
50 |             permission=access_type,
51 |             user_group_ids=user_group_ids,
52 |             db=db,
53 |         ):
54 |             return True
55 | 
56 |     knowledge_base_id = file.meta.get('collection_name') if file.meta else None
57 |     if knowledge_base_id:
58 |         knowledge_bases = await Knowledges.get_knowledge_bases_by_user_id(user.id, access_type, db=db)
59 |         for knowledge_base in knowledge_bases:
60 |             if knowledge_base.id == knowledge_base_id:
61 |                 return True
62 | 
63 |     # Check if the file is associated with any channels the user has access to
64 |     channels = await Channels.get_channels_by_file_id_and_user_id(file_id, user.id, db=db)
65 |     if access_type == 'read' and channels:
66 |         return True
67 | 
68 |     # Check if the file is associated with any chats the user has access to
69 |     shared_chat_ids = await Chats.get_shared_chat_ids_by_file_id(file_id, db=db)
70 |     if shared_chat_ids:
71 |         accessible_ids = await AccessGrants.get_accessible_resource_ids(
72 |             user_id=user.id,
73 |             resource_type='shared_chat',
74 |             resource_ids=shared_chat_ids,
75 |             permission='read',
76 |             user_group_ids=user_group_ids,
77 |             db=db,
78 |         )
79 |         if accessible_ids:
80 |             return True
81 | 
82 |     # Check if the file is directly attached to a shared workspace model
83 |     for model in await Models.get_models_by_user_id(user.id, permission=access_type, db=db):
84 |         knowledge_items = getattr(model.meta, 'knowledge', None) or []
85 |         for item in knowledge_items:
86 |             if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get('type') == 'file' and item.get('id') == file.id:
87 |                 return True
88 | 
89 |     return False

268 |     @staticmethod
269 |     def _glob_to_like_pattern(glob: str) -> str:
270 |         """
271 |         Convert a glob/fnmatch pattern to a SQL LIKE pattern.
272 | 
273 |         Escapes SQL special characters and converts glob wildcards:
274 |         - `*` becomes `%` (match any sequence of characters)
275 |         - `?` becomes `_` (match exactly one character)
276 | 
277 |         Args:
278 |             glob: A glob pattern (e.g., "*.txt", "file?.doc")
279 | 
280 |         Returns:
281 |             A SQL LIKE compatible pattern with proper escaping.
282 |         """
283 |         # Escape SQL special characters first, then convert glob wildcards
284 |         pattern = glob.replace('\\', '\\\\')
285 |         pattern = pattern.replace('%', '\\%')
286 |         pattern = pattern.replace('_', '\\_')
287 |         pattern = pattern.replace('*', '%')
288 |         pattern = pattern.replace('?', '_')
289 |         return pattern

import logging

from open_webui.models.users import UserModel
from open_webui.models.files import Files
from open_webui.models.knowledge import Knowledges
from open_webui.models.channels import Channels
from open_webui.models.chats import Chats
from open_webui.models.groups import Groups
from open_webui.models.models import Models
from open_webui.models.access_grants import AccessGrants

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


async def has_access_to_file(
    file_id: str | None,
    access_type: str,
    user: UserModel,
    db: AsyncSession | None = None,
) -> bool:
    """
    Check if a user has the specified access to a file through any of:
    - Knowledge bases (ownership or access grants)
    - Shared workspace models that attach the file directly
    - Channels the user is a member of
    - Shared chats

    NOTE: This does NOT check direct file ownership — callers should check
    file.user_id == user.id separately before calling this.
    """
    file = await Files.get_file_by_id(file_id, db=db)
    log.debug(f'Checking if user has {access_type} access to file')
    if not file:
        return False

    # Direct ownership
    if file.user_id == user.id:
        return True

    # Check if the file is associated with any knowledge bases the user has access to
    knowledge_bases = await Knowledges.get_knowledges_by_file_id(file_id, db=db)
    user_group_ids = {group.id for group in await Groups.get_groups_by_member_id(user.id, db=db)}
    for knowledge_base in knowledge_bases:
        if knowledge_base.user_id == user.id or await AccessGrants.has_access(
            user_id=user.id,
            resource_type='knowledge',
            resource_id=knowledge_base.id,
            permission=access_type,
            user_group_ids=user_group_ids,
            db=db,
        ):
            return True

    knowledge_base_id = file.meta.get('collection_name') if file.meta else None
    if knowledge_base_id:
        knowledge_bases = await Knowledges.get_knowledge_bases_by_user_id(user.id, access_type, db=db)
        for knowledge_base in knowledge_bases:
            if knowledge_base.id == knowledge_base_id:
                return True

    # Check if the file is associated with any channels the user has access to
    channels = await Channels.get_channels_by_file_id_and_user_id(file_id, user.id, db=db)
    if access_type == 'read' and channels:
        return True

    # Check if the file is associated with any chats the user has access to
    shared_chat_ids = await Chats.get_shared_chat_ids_by_file_id(file_id, db=db)
    if shared_chat_ids:
        accessible_ids = await AccessGrants.get_accessible_resource_ids(
            user_id=user.id,
            resource_type='shared_chat',
            resource_ids=shared_chat_ids,
            permission='read',
            user_group_ids=user_group_ids,
            db=db,
        )
        if accessible_ids:
            return True

    # Check if the file is directly attached to a shared workspace model
    for model in await Models.get_models_by_user_id(user.id, permission=access_type, db=db):
        knowledge_items = getattr(model.meta, 'knowledge', None) or []
        for item in knowledge_items:
            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get('type') == 'file' and item.get('id') == file.id:
                return True

    return False

    @staticmethod
    def _glob_to_like_pattern(glob: str) -> str:
        """
        Convert a glob/fnmatch pattern to a SQL LIKE pattern.

        Escapes SQL special characters and converts glob wildcards:
        - `*` becomes `%` (match any sequence of characters)
        - `?` becomes `_` (match exactly one character)

        Args:
            glob: A glob pattern (e.g., "*.txt", "file?.doc")

        Returns:
            A SQL LIKE compatible pattern with proper escaping.
        """
        # Escape SQL special characters first, then convert glob wildcards
        pattern = glob.replace('\\', '\\\\')
        pattern = pattern.replace('%', '\\%')
        pattern = pattern.replace('_', '\\_')
        pattern = pattern.replace('*', '%')
        pattern = pattern.replace('?', '_')
        return pattern

    async def search_files(
        self,
        user_id: Optional[str] = None,
        filename: str = '*',
        skip: int = 0,
        limit: int = 100,
        db: Optional[AsyncSession] = None,
    ) -> list[FileModel]:
        """
        Search files with glob pattern matching, optional user filter, and pagination.

        Args:
            user_id: Filter by user ID. If None, returns files for all users.
            filename: Glob pattern to match filenames (e.g., "*.txt"). Default "*" matches all.
            skip: Number of results to skip for pagination.
            limit: Maximum number of results to return.
            db: Optional database session.

        Returns:
            List of matching FileModel objects, ordered by created_at descending.
        """
        async with get_async_db_context(db) as db:
            stmt = select(File)

            if user_id:
                stmt = stmt.filter_by(user_id=user_id)

            pattern = self._glob_to_like_pattern(filename)
            if pattern != '%':
                stmt = stmt.filter(File.filename.ilike(pattern, escape='\\'))

            result = await db.execute(stmt.order_by(File.created_at.desc(), File.id.desc()).offset(skip).limit(limit))
            return [FileModel.model_validate(file) for file in result.scalars().all()]

    async def update_file_by_id(
        self, id: str, form_data: FileUpdateForm, db: Optional[AsyncSession] = None
    ) -> Optional[FileModel]:
        async with get_async_db_context(db) as db:
            try:
                result = await db.execute(select(File).filter_by(id=id))
                file = result.scalars().first()

                if form_data.hash is not None:
                    file.hash = form_data.hash

                if form_data.data is not None:
                    file.data = {**(file.data if file.data else {}), **form_data.data}

                if form_data.meta is not None:
                    file.meta = {**(file.meta if file.meta else {}), **form_data.meta}

import logging

from open_webui.models.users import UserModel
from open_webui.models.files import Files
from open_webui.models.knowledge import Knowledges
from open_webui.models.channels import Channels
from open_webui.models.chats import Chats
from open_webui.models.groups import Groups
from open_webui.models.models import Models
from open_webui.models.access_grants import AccessGrants

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


async def has_access_to_file(
    file_id: str | None,
    access_type: str,
    user: UserModel,
    db: AsyncSession | None = None,
) -> bool:
    """
    Check if a user has the specified access to a file through any of:
    - Knowledge bases (ownership or access grants)
    - Shared workspace models that attach the file directly
    - Channels the user is a member of
    - Shared chats

    NOTE: This does NOT check direct file ownership — callers should check
    file.user_id == user.id separately before calling this.
    """
    file = await Files.get_file_by_id(file_id, db=db)
    log.debug(f'Checking if user has {access_type} access to file')
    if not file:
        return False

    # Direct ownership
    if file.user_id == user.id:
        return True

    # Check if the file is associated with any knowledge bases the user has access to
    knowledge_bases = await Knowledges.get_knowledges_by_file_id(file_id, db=db)
    user_group_ids = {group.id for group in await Groups.get_groups_by_member_id(user.id, db=db)}
    for knowledge_base in knowledge_bases:
        if knowledge_base.user_id == user.id or await AccessGrants.has_access(
            user_id=user.id,
            resource_type='knowledge',
            resource_id=knowledge_base.id,
            permission=access_type,
            user_group_ids=user_group_ids,
            db=db,
        ):
            return True

    knowledge_base_id = file.meta.get('collection_name') if file.meta else None
    if knowledge_base_id:
        knowledge_bases = await Knowledges.get_knowledge_bases_by_user_id(user.id, access_type, db=db)
        for knowledge_base in knowledge_bases:
            if knowledge_base.id == knowledge_base_id:
                return True

    # Check if the file is associated with any channels the user has access to
    channels = await Channels.get_channels_by_file_id_and_user_id(file_id, user.id, db=db)
    if access_type == 'read' and channels:
        return True

    # Check if the file is associated with any chats the user has access to
    shared_chat_ids = await Chats.get_shared_chat_ids_by_file_id(file_id, db=db)
    if shared_chat_ids:
        accessible_ids = await AccessGrants.get_accessible_resource_ids(
            user_id=user.id,
            resource_type='shared_chat',
            resource_ids=shared_chat_ids,
            permission='read',
            user_group_ids=user_group_ids,
            db=db,
        )
        if accessible_ids:
            return True

    # Check if the file is directly attached to a shared workspace model
    for model in await Models.get_models_by_user_id(user.id, permission=access_type, db=db):
        knowledge_items = getattr(model.meta, 'knowledge', None) or []
        for item in knowledge_items:
            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get('type') == 'file' and item.get('id') == file.id:
                return True

    return False

    @staticmethod
    def _glob_to_like_pattern(glob: str) -> str:
        """
        Convert a glob/fnmatch pattern to a SQL LIKE pattern.

        Escapes SQL special characters and converts glob wildcards:
        - `*` becomes `%` (match any sequence of characters)
        - `?` becomes `_` (match exactly one character)

        Args:
            glob: A glob pattern (e.g., "*.txt", "file?.doc")

        Returns:
            A SQL LIKE compatible pattern with proper escaping.
        """
        # Escape SQL special characters first, then convert glob wildcards
        pattern = glob.replace('\\', '\\\\')
        pattern = pattern.replace('%', '\\%')
        pattern = pattern.replace('_', '\\_')
        pattern = pattern.replace('*', '%')
        pattern = pattern.replace('?', '_')
        return pattern

    async def search_files(
        self,
        user_id: Optional[str] = None,
        filename: str = '*',
        skip: int = 0,
        limit: int = 100,
        db: Optional[AsyncSession] = None,
    ) -> list[FileModel]:
        """
        Search files with glob pattern matching, optional user filter, and pagination.

        Args:
            user_id: Filter by user ID. If None, returns files for all users.
            filename: Glob pattern to match filenames (e.g., "*.txt"). Default "*" matches all.
            skip: Number of results to skip for pagination.
            limit: Maximum number of results to return.
            db: Optional database session.

        Returns:
            List of matching FileModel objects, ordered by created_at descending.
        """
        async with get_async_db_context(db) as db:
            stmt = select(File)

            if user_id:
                stmt = stmt.filter_by(user_id=user_id)

            pattern = self._glob_to_like_pattern(filename)
            if pattern != '%':
                stmt = stmt.filter(File.filename.ilike(pattern, escape='\\'))

            result = await db.execute(stmt.order_by(File.created_at.desc(), File.id.desc()).offset(skip).limit(limit))
            return [FileModel.model_validate(file) for file in result.scalars().all()]

    async def update_file_by_id(
        self, id: str, form_data: FileUpdateForm, db: Optional[AsyncSession] = None
    ) -> Optional[FileModel]:
        async with get_async_db_context(db) as db:
            try:
                result = await db.execute(select(File).filter_by(id=id))
                file = result.scalars().first()

                if form_data.hash is not None:
                    file.hash = form_data.hash

                if form_data.data is not None:
                    file.data = {**(file.data if file.data else {}), **form_data.data}

                if form_data.meta is not None:
                    file.meta = {**(file.meta if file.meta else {}), **form_data.meta}

result.scope: open-webui/open-webui@841c9045d789005145274955e7ef60b1b11a9be9; allowed source scope backend/open_webui; behavior analysis of process_file at the retrieval router's /process/file route

observations.subject: process_file route
observations.claim: The entry is POST /process/file in retrieval.py, included by main.py under the /api/v1/retrieval router prefix; the handler requires form_data and a verified user dependency.

observations.subject: verified caller
observations.claim: The caller is the user object supplied by Depends(get_verified_user); the handler branches on user.role and uses user.id for non-admin file selection.

observations.subject: supplied file_id
observations.claim: The supplied form_data.file_id selects the file. Admin callers fetch by file ID alone; non-admin callers fetch by file ID together with user.id, so the non-admin lookup is directly owner-bound.

observations.subject: file existence and caller branch
observations.claim: Processing proceeds only if the selected file is truthy. Admin role permits lookup without an owner predicate; all other roles use the owner-constrained lookup. A missing or unauthorized non-admin selection reaches the same visible not-found response branch.

observations.subject: destination collection_name
observations.claim: The destination is form_data.collection_name when supplied; otherwise it is derived as file-{file.id}. The supplied collection name is not used in the file-selection guard.

observations.subject: processing and vector write
observations.claim: After file selection, the handler builds documents from supplied content, previously stored vector content, a loader over file.path, or file.data. It updates the selected file's content/status/hash and, when embedding/retrieval is enabled, calls save_docs_to_vector_db with the selected collection_name and metadata containing the selected file.id; that function ultimately inserts vector items into that collection.

observations.subject: shared-file access helper
observations.claim: retrieval.py imports has_access_to_file, but the visible process_file body does not call it. The helper itself supports ownership and several sharing relationships, but its documented use is not evidenced on this path.

observations.subject: same selected file
observations.claim: The input object is the file selected from form_data.file_id. The handler uses that same file.id for document metadata, file-data updates, final metadata/status/hash updates, and the vector-write metadata.

observations.subject: collection versus file
observations.claim: The file identity and collection identity are distinct: file.id identifies the authorized/selected file, while collection_name may be caller-supplied and may name a collection unrelated by source-visible authorization to that file.

observations.subject: output target
observations.claim: The protected input object and file-record effects are the same selected file, but the vector effect targets the separately chosen collection_name. Therefore input-file identity and all output targets are not uniformly the same object.

observations.subject: ownership scenarios
observations.claim: Both scenarios enter the same POST handler and are subject to the admin/non-admin file lookup branch before processing.

observations.subject: caller-owned file
observations.claim: For a non-admin caller whose user.id equals the file's owner identity used by get_file_by_id_and_user_id, the file is selected and processing can continue, subject to the later processing and configuration conditions.

observations.subject: file owned by another user
observations.claim: For a non-admin caller and a file owned by another user, the owner-constrained lookup does not select that file on the visible path, so the handler raises HTTP 404 and does not reach processing or vector insertion. The source does not show a sharing/access-grant exception in this handler.

observations.subject: admin caller
observations.claim: An admin caller is an explicit exception: the handler fetches by file ID without the non-admin owner predicate, so an existing file owned by another user can proceed. This does not establish any destination-collection ownership or authorization.

observations.subject: destination collection
observations.claim: Caller ownership of the file does not imply ownership of form_data.collection_name. The visible process_file path does not check collection ownership or collection access before passing the name to vector operations.

observations.subject: successful owned-file path
observations.claim: When processing succeeds, the selected file record is updated and vector items can be inserted into the supplied collection or the derived file-{file.id} collection, depending on the request and configuration.

observations.subject: content and collection branches
observations.claim: Visible branches are: supplied content takes precedence and deletes the file-{file.id} async vector collection before rebuilding docs; a supplied collection without content first queries file-{file.id} for prior content and otherwise uses file.data; with neither, the handler loads from storage when file.path exists or uses file.data.

observations.subject: bypass configuration
observations.claim: If BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is enabled, the handler updates file status/hash and returns success without calling save_docs_to_vector_db; the returned collection_name is None.

observations.subject: vector-write conditions
observations.claim: When bypass is disabled, save_docs_to_vector_db may return early if the destination collection already exists and add is false; add is true only when form_data.collection_name was supplied. Otherwise it generates embeddings and inserts items into the named collection.

observations.subject: duplicate and content limits
observations.claim: The vector helper checks an existing document hash and raises a duplicate-content error when the existing metadata file_id differs; empty post-split documents and invalid splitter configuration also fail before insertion.

observations.subject: failure behavior
observations.claim: Processing exceptions update the selected file status to failed and clear its hash, then return an HTTP 400 for the visible handler-level error path; a missing selected file returns HTTP 404.

observations.subject: authorization limits
observations.claim: The visible authorization limit is file selection by admin role or exact caller ownership lookup for non-admins. No destination collection authorization, collection-owner binding, or invocation of the imported generalized file-access helper is shown in this path.

result.scope: open-webui/open-webui@841c9045d789005145274955e7ef60b1b11a9be9; allowed source scope backend/open_webui; behavior analysis of the retrieval router's process_file endpoint, mounted as POST /api/v1/retrieval/process/file

behavior.explanation: The endpoint binds the caller through Depends(get_verified_user), then authorizes selection of the supplied file_id by role: admins look up any file by ID, while non-admins use a lookup constrained by both file_id and user.id. If a file is selected, the destination is the supplied collection_name or the derived name file-{file.id}. The handler processes content and updates the selected file; unless retrieval is bypassed, it passes that destination to the vector helper, which can insert vectors there. No destination-collection authorization check is visible in the traced flow.

observations.subject: process_file route
observations.claim: The entry is POST /process/file on the retrieval router, mounted under /api/v1/retrieval; it receives ProcessFileForm and Depends(get_verified_user).

observations.subject: verified caller
observations.claim: The handler receives a user from get_verified_user, branches on user.role, and binds non-admin file selection to user.id.

observations.subject: file and destination
observations.claim: form_data.file_id selects the input file; collection_name is independently supplied or derived as file-{file.id}.

observations.subject: role-specific file selection
observations.claim: Admins fetch by file ID alone; non-admins fetch by file ID and user.id. Processing requires a truthy selected file; otherwise the endpoint returns HTTP 404.

observations.subject: selected file and vector collection
observations.claim: The selected file receives content/status/hash/metadata updates, and when retrieval is enabled the separately selected collection_name can receive vector items carrying the selected file.id in metadata.

observations.subject: admin and generalized file access
observations.claim: Admin bypasses the non-admin owner-constrained lookup. Although retrieval.py imports has_access_to_file, the visible process_file body does not call it.

observations.subject: selected input file
observations.claim: The input object is the file selected from form_data.file_id under the role-specific lookup.

observations.subject: caller-to-file relation
observations.claim: For non-admins the caller's user.id participates in selecting the file; admins are the role exception.

observations.subject: file identity versus collection identity
observations.claim: The selected file.id and destination collection_name are distinct identifiers, and collection_name may be caller-supplied.

observations.subject: output targets
observations.claim: File-record effects target the selected file, while vector insertion targets collection_name; vector metadata links the inserted items back to file.id.

observations.subject: ownership scenarios
observations.claim: Both caller-owned and other-user-file scenarios enter the same verified-user endpoint and encounter the admin/non-admin lookup branch first.

observations.subject: non-admin caller-owned file
observations.claim: A non-admin lookup includes both form_data.file_id and user.id, binding file selection to the caller identity on the visible path.

observations.subject: other user's file
observations.claim: If the non-admin owner-constrained lookup does not select the supplied file, processing is short-circuited with HTTP 404.

observations.subject: admin caller
observations.claim: An admin selects an existing file by ID without the visible owner predicate and can therefore proceed with an other-user file.

observations.subject: destination collection
observations.claim: File ownership does not establish ownership of the supplied collection_name, and no destination ownership/access check is visible before vector operations.

observations.subject: successful selected-file path
observations.claim: A successful path updates the selected file and may write vectors into either the supplied collection or file-{file.id}.

observations.subject: verified process_file entry
observations.claim: The route requires the verified-user dependency and a form containing file_id, with optional content and collection_name.

observations.subject: caller role and ID
observations.claim: The visible authorization choice is controlled by user.role, and non-admin selection uses user.id.

observations.subject: processing source and destination
observations.claim: The selected file supplies stored data/path and metadata; request content can replace the processing source, while collection_name independently determines the vector destination.

observations.subject: processing and vector conditions
observations.claim: Visible guards include content-source branching, bypass configuration, duplicate hash/file-id comparison, splitter validity, nonempty documents, collection existence with add behavior, and successful embedding/vector operations.

observations.subject: success and failure effects
observations.claim: Success updates file state and may insert vectors; bypass omits vector insertion. Processing failures mark the file failed and clear its hash, while an unselected file produces HTTP 404.

observations.subject: visible authorization limits
observations.claim: No destination collection authorization or invocation of has_access_to_file is visible in process_file; concrete backend tenancy and runtime configuration remain unverified.
